prompt: What does a service perimeter decide that IAM does not?

choices.text: How much an API call costs
choices.why: Perimeters say nothing about price.

choices.text: Origins and destinations
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: Which roles a service account holds
choices.why: That is IAM.

choices.text: Which images may run
choices.why: That is Binary Authorization.

prompt: A stolen token with the right role is used from another country to read an export. What happens with the perimeter enforced?

choices.text: Allowed, and logged as a violation
choices.why: That is dry run, not enforcement.

choices.text: Allowed: IAM says yes
choices.why: The perimeter refuses whatever IAM says.

choices.text: Refused: outside, no access level matches
choices.why: Right. The third row of the table.

choices.text: Refused only for BigQuery, not for Cloud Storage
choices.why: Both are restricted.

prompt: A script inside the project, with every permission, copies exports to a bucket in an unknown project. What stops it?

choices.text: The access level for the office
choices.why: Access levels admit requests; egress rules let data out.

choices.text: Nothing: it is inside the perimeter
choices.why: Inside callers still cannot send data out.

choices.text: IAM, because the unknown bucket refuses it
choices.why: The thief's bucket would happily accept.

choices.text: No egress rule allows data out to that project
choices.why: Right. Exfiltration is the fourth row.

prompt: Why does the egress rule name one identity, one project and one method?
hint: Each rule is a path out.

choices.text: Rules accept no wildcards at all
choices.why: Some fields accept broad values; the point is not to use them.

choices.text: Because the partner's project is in another region
choices.why: Regions are not the concern of an egress rule.

choices.text: To keep the perimeter free of charge
choices.why: It is free either way.

choices.text: So the hole is the size of one job
choices.why: Right. Never *.

prompt: Who can create the access policy that holds perimeters?

choices.text: The service account of the API
choices.why: It is a member of the perimeter, not its author.

choices.text: Somebody with an organisation-level role
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: Nobody: Google creates it
choices.why: It is created like any other resource, by an organisation admin.

choices.text: Any project owner
choices.why: A project owner cannot act on the organisation.

prompt: In dry run, what happens to a request the perimeter would refuse?

choices.text: It is held for approval
choices.why: Nothing waits for a person.

choices.text: It is silently dropped
choices.why: Dry run refuses nothing.

choices.text: Allowed and logged
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: It is refused with 403
choices.why: That is enforcement.

prompt: A dry-run violation shows a nightly job in another project reading the exports, legitimately. What do you do?

choices.text: Remove Cloud Storage from the restricted services
choices.why: That removes the protection for everybody.

choices.text: Enforce anyway; the job will adapt
choices.why: It will break, and somebody will find out the hard way.

choices.text: Write a narrow ingress rule for it
choices.why: Right. Narrow, explicit, reviewed.

choices.text: Open an incident
choices.why: It is legitimate; incidents are for what nobody can explain.

prompt: Somebody reports "permission denied, but I have the role" after enforcement. What do you ask for first?

choices.text: A screenshot of the IAM page
choices.why: They already say they have the role.

choices.text: Which browser they use
choices.why: Irrelevant to which control refused.

choices.text: The error's unique id
choices.why: Right. The audit log names the rule that refused.

choices.text: Their password
choices.why: Never ask for a password, and it would not help.

prompt: Put the introduction of the perimeter in order.
items: Write the perimeter in spec, in dry run
Read a week of dry-run violations
Add access levels and rules for the legitimate ones
Move the configuration to status, enforced
trap: Enforcing before reading is the slip: the legitimate jobs find out by breaking.

prompt: Match each part of the configuration to what it is.

pairs.right: a named condition on a request's origin
a line around projects and restricted services

right_distractors: a key that wraps data keys

prompt: The Terraform block holding the perimeter's dry-run configuration is `___`.
hint: Four letters; status is the enforced one.

prompt: Which of these does the perimeter allow? Choose all that apply.
hint: Inside, the access level, and the one egress rule.

choices.text: The API reading an export from Cloud Run in the project
choices.why: Yes, inside.

choices.text: A person at the office downloading an export
choices.why: Yes, the access level.

choices.text: A copy to an unknown project's bucket
choices.why: No, exfiltration.

choices.text: The export job writing to the partner's bucket
choices.why: Yes, the egress rule.
